title: What ends up in the bucket

sections.title: Key prefix
sections.text: Every key starts with the destination's Prefix, then the block's Key prefix. <prefix> stands for both. With both blank, keys start at the bucket's root.

sections.title: Upload to Bucket
sections.text: Key Holds <prefix>/<path inside Source> One object per file, with folders kept as key segments. <prefix>/<file name> The object for a Source that is a single file. The block deletes nothing. An object that exists at the same size is skipped, and any other is replaced.

sections.title: Publish DH Snapshot
sections.text: Key Holds Replaced or deleted <prefix>/latest.json A pointer to the newest snapshot's index.json: its format, createdAt and the path. Rewritten by each publish, as its last write. <prefix>/snapshots/<stamp>/index.json The snapshot: Distant Horizons version, server folder, and for each level its folder, size, SHA-256 and parts. Deleted with its snapshot. <prefix>/snapshots/<stamp>/index.html With Download page on: the download page, listing each level's file with its size and the folder to put it in. Deleted with its snapshot. <prefix>/snapshots/<stamp>/<level folder>/DistantHorizons.sqlite With Download page on: one level's whole database, built inside the bucket from its parts. Deleted with its snapshot. <prefix>/parts/<sha256> A slice of a database, named by its SHA-256 and up to 8 MiB, shared by every snapshot that uses it. Deleted when no kept snapshot lists it. <stamp> is the snapshot's UTC time, such as 20261012T040000Z. <level folder> is <levelKeyPrefix>@<namespace>@@<path>, such as myserver@minecraft@@overworld. <prefix>/ latest.jsonpoints at the newest snapshot snapshots/ 20261012T040000Z/one snapshot index.json index.htmlwith Download page on myserver@minecraft@@overworld/with Download page on DistantHorizons.sqlite parts/ <sha256>a slice of a database

sections.title: Private link
sections.text: Key Holds <prefix>/<token>/latest.json The pointer, as in the public layout. <prefix>/<token>/snapshots/<stamp>/… The same snapshot files as in the public layout. <prefix>/parts/<sha256> The parts, which stay where they are. <token> is 26 random lowercase letters and digits. The destination's Snapshot link row switches between the two layouts. <prefix>/ <token>/26 random lowercase letters and digits latest.json snapshots/ 20261012T040000Z/ parts/stay where they are

sections.title: Deletions
sections.text: When Deletes A publish finishes Snapshots beyond the newest Snapshots to keep, except the one latest.json points at. Then every part no kept snapshot lists. The next publish after a cut-off one A folder without index.json, once it is older than the oldest snapshot kept. The link switches or rotates The old address's latest.json first, then its whole snapshots/ folder. Only the snapshot latest.json points at moves to the new address. A destination is deleted in Settings Nothing in the bucket. A cleanup only touches folders named like a stamp and parts named like a SHA-256. If it cannot read what it needs, it deletes nothing, and the publish reports a warning. The next publish cleans up again.

title: Cron expressions
lead: The Cron Schedule block fires when the clock matches a five-field expression.

sections.title: Fields
sections.text: Field Values Minute 0 to 59 Hour 0 to 23 Day of month 1 to 31 Month 1 to 12 Day of week 0 to 6, where 0 is Sunday Write the five fields in that order, separated by spaces. The block checks the clock at the start of each minute. It uses the time zone of this computer. Day of month and day of week must both match. A block fires at most once a minute, and only while its graph is on.

sections.title: Syntax
sections.text: Form Example Means Any value * Every value of the field. Value 30 Exactly that value. Range 9-17 Every value from the first to the second, both included. List 0,15,45 Any listed value. An item can be a value or a range. Step */10 Every value divisible by the step. Day of month */10 is the 10th, 20th and 30th.

sections.title: Examples
sections.text: Expression Runs * * * * * Every minute. */5 * * * * Every 5 minutes, on the minutes 0, 5, 10 and so on. 0 * * * * At the start of every hour. 0,30 * * * * At the start and the middle of every hour. 30 9 * * * Every day at 09:30. 0 */6 * * * At 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00. 0 4 * * 1-5 At 04:00 from Monday to Friday. 0 0 * * 0 At midnight on Sunday. 0 12 1 * * At 12:00 on the 1st of each month. 15 3 1 1 * At 03:15 on 1 January. 0 9 13 * 5 At 09:00 on a day that is both the 13th and a Friday. 00:000 */6 * * * fires 06:00 fires 12:00 fires 18:00 fires

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Heads up An expression the parser cannot read never matches, and nothing reports it. An expression that does not have five fields never matches. Names such as MON or JAN, macros such as @hourly, and 7 for Sunday are not read. A step works only as */n, so 1-5/2 and 5/15 never match. A range that wraps, such as 22-2, never matches. The next run is looked up 14 days ahead. A rarer schedule shows no next run time.

title: FAQ
lead: Short answers about Konnekt, servers and updates.

sections.title: Konnekt
sections.text: Is it free? Yes, under the MIT licence: keep the copyright notice, and the rest is yours. No accounts, no tiers, no subscriptions. Does it phone home? No telemetry, analytics or crash reporting. On its own it contacts GitHub, to check for updates. Everything else follows something you set up: Modrinth for mods CurseForge once you add an API key NeoForge's Maven for a loader Your buckets Cloudflare for a tunnel Any address an HTTP Request block names Where does it store my data? Your server files stay where they are. Konnekt's own state (servers, layouts, presets, scheduled tasks) is JSON in the OS application-data directory. Is it stable? It's alpha. The core is functional and in daily use, but expect rough edges. The roadmap has what is next.

sections.title: Servers
sections.text: Which server types work? Vanilla, Paper, Spigot and Bukkit, and modded Fabric, Forge and NeoForge. The loader is detected automatically. Bedrock is not supported. Why does the server stop as soon as I start it? On a first run that is almost always the EULA. Minecraft will not start until you have accepted it, and says so in the log on its way out. Konnekt watches for that line and offers to write eula.txt for you, then starts the server again. Can I manage a server on another machine? No, Konnekt manages servers on the machine it runs on. Remote Access opens that machine's dashboard in a browser elsewhere.

sections.title: Updates
sections.text: Can I run the newest code? Yes: snapshots are built from the newest code whenever it changes, and published as pre-releases. They're untested, so Konnekt warns before installing one. Take the first from the download page. After that a snapshot offers you the next one itself, and a release once one overtakes it. To follow snapshots from a stable build, switch the channel in Settings, General.

title: How a graph runs
lead: A graph is a set of wired blocks that a trigger starts and that then run one at a time.

sections.title: What starts a run
sections.text: A graph belongs to the server it was built on. A server can have any number of graphs. A graph fires only while it is switched on. A new graph starts off, and run works on a graph that is off. Time triggers check the clock once a minute, whether or not the server is running. Event triggers fire when their own server reports the event. They wait out their Cooldown (seconds) between firings. Heads up Graphs run only while Konnekt is open. Closing Konnekt stops the scheduler, and stops a running server too. A time that passes while it is closed is not made up. Cron Schedule0 4 * * * onComplete Create BackupFull server

sections.title: Control and data
sections.text: Control wires set the order. Each block leaves by one control port, such as onComplete or onTrue, and only the blocks wired to it run next. Blocks wired to the same port run one after another, in an order not to rely on. Chain them with a wire when the order matters. A block that no control wire reaches never runs. Data wires carry values. A wired value replaces the block's own field. A wire that has no value yet leaves the field in use. Blocks with no control ports, such as Read Attribute, Constant and Math, run when a block that needs their value runs. They run once per run, and every block wired to them gets that value. The outputs of other blocks, such as the Backup filename of Create Backup, exist once that block has run. A block wired to one that has not run yet reads nothing. Cron Schedule0 4 * * * onComplete ConditionA == 0 Read Attributeplayers.count onTrue Create BackupFull server

sections.title: Failures and limits
sections.text: A block that fails leaves by onFailed, and the blocks wired there run. With nothing wired there, that branch ends and the other branches carry on. The run is marked failed either way, with the reason of the first failure. It raises a Run failed bubble and adds it to Notifications. A graph runs once at a time. A trigger that fires during a run starts nothing, and is not queued. Different graphs run at the same time. Limit Value One block 60 s, longer for the upload and Distant Horizons blocks One run 30 minutes, or longer when its blocks have longer limits Block executions in a run 500, which ends a loop CommandRestart Server onComplete NotifyBack up onFailed NotifyRestart failed

sections.title: Tunnel
sections.text: Reach it from anywhere opens a Cloudflare quick tunnel to the dashboard. It needs Remote access on first, and says Switch remote access on first. until then. Heads up Cloudflare sits between the browser and Konnekt and can read the traffic, your password included. Konnekt runs cloudflared, Cloudflare's tunnel program, with tunnel --no-autoupdate --url http://127.0.0.1:port. It downloads a fixed release from the cloudflare/cloudflared releases on GitHub when it has no verified copy. Konnekt checks the file's size and SHA-256 against values built into the app, before every run. The file lives in the bin folder of the data directory. Konnekt knows the download for Windows x86-64 and for Linux x86-64 and ARM64. The tunnel's address ends in trycloudflare.com, with a QR code for a phone camera. The address is new every time the tunnel starts. A device approved through it is forgotten when the tunnel closes, and is approved again on the next one. Switching Remote access off closes the tunnel, and so does its idle switch-off. If the tunnel is not up within 45 seconds, the pane shows The tunnel did not open. and the last lines cloudflared printed. Your own address Your own address is a named tunnel on your own Cloudflare account. Its address stays the same across runs, and a device approved through it stays approved. Claude connectors need it. In the Cloudflare dashboard, create a tunnel. Route a hostname you own to http://127.0.0.1:port, with a port from 1024 to 65535. Copy the tunnel's token. In Konnekt, fill in Hostname, Port and Tunnel token, then press Save. Switch on Remote access, then Reach it from anywhere. Field What it does Default Hostname The name you routed, such as dash.example.net, with at least two labels and no wildcard, scheme, port or path. None Port The port your route points at, from 1024 to 65535. Remote access listens on it while the address is saved. None Tunnel token The token from Cloudflare, kept in its own file and passed to cloudflared as a file path. None The token is never shown again, and a blank field on a later save keeps the stored one. Change and Forget token are locked while a tunnel runs. Forget token deletes the token, the hostname and the port, and removes the devices approved on that hostname. Reach it from anywhere then opens a quick tunnel again. A named tunnel counts as up once cloudflared registers a connection, and the address is https:// and your hostname. Error Do the hostname is not a DNS name: use a name like dash.example.net Enter a name such as dash.example.net in Hostname. the tunnel token is not usable: paste the whole token, without spaces or line breaks Paste the whole token again. remote access is not listening on the named tunnel's port: it listens on address and the tunnel expects port port; switch remote access off and on Switch Remote access off and on, and the listener moves to the saved port. sections.title: Claude
sections.text: Claude on this computer lets Claude Code and Claude Desktop on this computer use Konnekt's tools. It is off by default, and it works without Remote access. Switch on Claude on this computer. For Claude Code, copy the line beside Claude Code and run it in a terminal. For Claude Desktop, copy the Claude Desktop config entry and merge it into the mcpServers object of Claude Desktop's config file. Note Konnekt opens a second listener on 127.0.0.1, guarded by a secret it makes at every start. Claude starts konnekt mcp, a small bridge program, which forwards each call to that listener. The bridge lists the tools even when Konnekt is closed. The Claude Code line is claude mcp add --transport stdio konnekt -- path mcp. The entry is a konnekt server whose command is that path and whose args is ["mcp"]. The path is the Konnekt executable that is running. While it listens, the pane reads Listening on an address, and Register Konnekt once; Claude finds it again after a restart. If it reads Not listening., switch it off and on again, or check konnekt.log. A call while Konnekt is closed fails with Konnekt is not running, or "Allow Claude on this computer" is off in its Settings. What Claude can do Group Tools See list_servers, server_status, server_summary, players, stats_history, console_tail, server_log, last_stop, backups, worlds, schedules, schedule_next_runs, config_files, config_file and mods Operate start_server, stop_server, restart_server, kick_player, ban_player, pardon_player, create_backup and run_schedule Console send_command: every call waits for you to press Allow once, and is refused if you do not No tool force stops a server, restores or deletes a backup, changes a world or removes a mod. No tool edits a server's settings or files either. Console lines, player names, ban reasons and world names reach Claude marked as text that players wrote. Claude connectors Claude connectors let claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code reach the same tools through the internet. They are off by default. The switch stays off until a password is set, with Set the password below first. beside it. It then waits for Your own address, with Set up your own address under Tunnel first. beside it. A quick tunnel is not enough, because its address changes. Save Your own address. Switch on Remote access, then Reach it from anywhere. Switch on Claude connectors. In claude.ai or Claude Desktop, add a connector and paste the connector URL. In Claude Code, run the line beside Claude Code. The connector URL is https://, your hostname and /mcp. It answers only while Remote access and the tunnel are on. The Claude Code line is claude mcp add --transport http konnekt url. While the switch is on and an own address is saved, the 30-minute idle switch-off is held back. The title bar then adds Claude to its label. Signing in a connector Claude opens a Konnekt page called Connect and the client's name. Tick the permissions. Type the Remote Access password and press Allow. Press Allow on the dialog on the desktop, which reads wants to connect to Konnekt. Note See your servers, players, console and schedules is ticked, and Start, stop and restart servers, run commands and manage players is not. The page waits for the desktop and checks again every two seconds. It expires after five minutes, and a connector has no device code to type. A connector that holds only the first permission signs in again when it needs the second. Both permissions are offered at every sign-in, whatever the client asked for, so a reconnected client can add the second. Konnekt accepts sign-ins from Claude's own clients only. Connected clients lists each one with its name and the host it was sent back to. Each reads Sees and operates servers or Sees servers, players, console and schedules. It also shows when the client connected and Last used, or Not used yet. Until one signs in, the list reads None yet. Revoke ends one client's access at its next call. Revoke all appears when two or more are connected, and each signs in again from scratch. Konnekt holds at most 16 connectors. A 17th sign-in is refused on the sign-in page until one is revoked. A connector ends 90 days after you approved it, or 30 days after its last use. Changing the password ends every connector. sections.title: Password
sections.text: The password is 12 to 256 characters. Konnekt keeps only an argon2id hash of it. Changing it signs every device out, and ends every Claude connector. Devices stay approved and sign in again with the new password. A browser that types five wrong passwords in a row must wait. The wait starts at 5 seconds, doubles with each miss and tops out at 15 minutes. A device that is already approved has its own count. An hour without a miss clears it. sections.title: Approved devices
sections.text: A signed in tag marks a device with a live session. Remove forgets the device and ends its sessions, so its next sign-in needs approval again. Sign out everywhere ends every session, and devices stay approved. A session ends after an hour without use, or 12 hours after sign-in. A browser remembers its approval for a year. A device name is 1 to 40 printable characters, and no two devices share one. At most 16 devices can be approved. Error Do The request was declined or has expired. Sign in again. title: Tiles
lead: Eleven tiles that show and control the selected server.

sections.title: Console
sections.text: Shows the selected server's log as it arrives. Type a command in the field and press Send once the server is running. clr clears the log. The arrow at the top left opens a search box and a level filter: All, Warn or Error. Maximized, it adds a Commands rail beside the log. Tip Timestamps and the number of lines kept are set in Console. Console commandSendclr

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Shows the server's state, then Players, TPS, Uptime and Memory. The state reads Online, Offline, Starting, Stopping or Unreachable. Maximized, it rolls up other tiles. It charts the last hour of CPU, RAM and players. Short views of Players, Active world, Backups and Schedules follow. Each short view has a button that opens its own tile. Overview only reads from the other tiles and changes nothing in them.

sections.title: Players
sections.text: Shows how many players are online and lists them with their operator level. Click a player for their status, OP level, whitelist entry and ban reason. There, kick and ban work on online players and take an optional reason. pardon appears for a banned player. The list refreshes when anyone joins or leaves, and when the server starts or stops. Maximized, it adds a search box and sorting by Name or OP level.

sections.title: Commands
sections.text: Shows one button per command, and a click runs it on the selected server. A first launch adds six: Start, Stop, Restart, Force Stop, Save All and TPS. Force Stop always asks first. Stop and Restart ask when Confirm before stopping is on in General. Maximized, it lists every button to rename, edit, copy, delete and reorder. Add one by typing a command, picking a preset, or linking a saved command from Kommands.

sections.title: Performance
sections.text: Shows TPS, CPU and RAM with a chart of recent samples. Konnekt takes a sample every 10 seconds and keeps the last hour. Maximized, the chart covers 5m, 15m or 1h. Click a series in its legend to hide it. A table lists each sample, sortable by any column, with a min·avg·max row.

sections.title: Scheduler
sections.text: Shows how many graphs are armed and when the next one runs. Maximized, it opens the graph editor. Graphs are covered in How a graph runs and Scheduler editor.

sections.title: Worlds
sections.text: Shows how many worlds the server has, their total size and which one is active. Maximized, it draws each world as a planet in a 3D scene. Click one to open its card: set active, backup, open folder, rename, duplicate and delete. set active on a running server offers to stop it first, and to start it again after. delete is missing for the active world and off while the server runs. The card also lists the world's backups, each with restore and delete.

sections.title: Backups
sections.text: Shows Last full backup, its size and how many archives are kept. Back up now takes a full server backup. On a running server it asks whether to back up now or stop the server first. Maximized, it lists backups under Server and Worlds. Each can be renamed, tagged and deleted. restore needs the server stopped. schedule opens the Scheduler, where the Backup block runs backups on a timer. Backups Last full backup Back up now

sections.title: Config
sections.text: Shows the MOTD as players see it, then the main server.properties values, as many as fit. The rest are counted in the last cell, and the RCON password is hidden. Click an on/off value to flip it, and a value with fixed choices to cycle through them. Double-click any other value to edit it. Each change is written to the file at once. Maximized, it lists the server, plugin and mod config files, with a search box. A file opens in a Form or Raw editor, with Save and Revert. A file the form cannot edit safely opens as Raw only. Note On a running server, changes apply after a restart.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.text: Lists events as they happen: joins, info, warnings, errors and crashes. The filter at the top left narrows it to Joins, Info, Warn or Errors. Clear all empties the list. It keeps the latest 200 until Konnekt closes. Tip Which events also raise a bubble or a desktop alert is set in Notifications.

sections.title: Plugins
sections.text: Lists the server's installed plugins, or its mods on a server that does not load plugins, as many as fit. A green dot is on, a grey one is off, and an orange one has an update. What does not fit is counted in the last cell. While the server runs, the tile says restart needed for changes. Maximized, each one switches on or off, by renaming its file between .jar and .jar.disabled. Add Content searches Modrinth, or CurseForge once you add an API key in Settings, and installs from it. A mod whose author allows downloads on CurseForge only links to its page there instead. Add Files adds jars from this computer, in the desktop app.

title: Warn, then restart every 6 hours
lead: Tell players a restart is coming, then restart the server every 6 hours.

sections.title: Before you start
sections.text: Konnekt left openGraphs run only while Konnekt is open. The 6-hour timer lives in memory, so closing Konnekt resets it. The scheduler editorMaximize the Scheduler tile to open it.

sections.title: What you build
sections.text: Five blocks that warn twice, then restart the server every 6 hours. Interval360 minutes onComplete Commandsay The server restarts in 1 minute. onComplete Delay 50 s onComplete Commandsay The server restarts in 10 seconds. onComplete Delay 10 s onComplete CommandRestart Server -60 ssay The server restarts in 1 minute -10 ssay The server restarts in 10 seconds 0Restart Server

sections.title: Add the trigger
sections.text: Open the editor and select Open blocks. Under trigger, click Interval. Set Interval (minutes) to 360. Note The first check that sees the graph on starts the timer. The first restart comes 6 hours after that. For fixed times, use Cron Schedule with 0 */6 * * * instead. Interval360 minutes

sections.title: Warn the players
sections.text: Add two Command blocks and two Delay blocks. On the first Command, set Command to say The server restarts in 1 minute. On the first Delay, set Seconds to 50. On the second Command, set Command to say The server restarts in 10 seconds. On the second Delay, set Seconds to 10. Drag from onComplete on Interval to trigger on the first Command. Wire each remaining block's onComplete to the next block's trigger, in the order of steps 2 to 5. Note One Delay waits 60 seconds at most, and a longer wait fails. For an earlier warning, chain more Delay blocks. Interval360 minutes onComplete Commandsay The server restarts in 1 minute. onComplete Delay 50 s onComplete Commandsay The server restarts in 10 seconds. onComplete Delay 10 s

sections.title: Add the restart
sections.text: Add a third Command. Set Command to Restart Server. Drag from onComplete on the last Delay to trigger on the new Command. Note It stops the server, waits for it to exit, and starts it again. The editor may warn that RCON is not confirmed for this block. The say lines already warn players through the console. A warning does not stop the graph from saving or running. Interval360 minutes onComplete Commandsay The server restarts in 1 minute. onComplete Delay 50 s onComplete Commandsay The server restarts in 10 seconds. onComplete Delay 10 s onComplete CommandRestart Server

sections.title: Switch it on
sections.text: Select Graph actions, then Save. Select [off] so it reads [on]. Heads up run starts the graph at once: the warnings go out, and the server restarts a minute later. Note A new graph starts off, and nothing fires until it is on.
